html: The Arabela are a small Indigenous people of the Peruvian Amazon who live on the Arabela River, a tributary of the Curaray, in the Loreto region of Peru. Their language belongs to the Zaparoan family, like those of the Iquito and the Sápara of Ecuador, and today few people speak it. Like other peoples of the area, they suffered from slave raids and disease during the rubber boom around 1900. Missionaries settled among them in the mid 1900s. They number a few hundred people.
